title: Handlebar Remote
tagline: A slim thumb controller between the grip and the switch cube, for the dash and your phone
summary: One slim collar on the left handlebar, between the grip and the bike's switch cube: a 5-way joystick with 2 buttons either side of it in a row on top, tilted toward the grip under your thumb, and the electronics in a slim bay underneath. It works the Handlebar Dash over its own wiring (one of the dash's expansion slots) and a phone or anything else over Bluetooth, as a keyboard with media keys. One smooth, rounded body. The controls' top is a thumb cradle (curved along the thumb's sweep, each button in its own cup, ridges between them, the joystick standing up in the middle), a single cover with no screws on the face, sealed by a printed TPU keypad that is also the gasket of its one low seam. General purpose: the bar size, the gap and the angles are settings.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). The switches and boards have no published drawings: measure yours first, and the gap you can make between the grip and the switch cube. The firmware comes next.
see_sub: One smooth pebble-shaped collar, 19 mm wide, in a 20 mm gap between the grip and the switch cube (slide the cube inboard to make it): the controls on top, tilted 20 degrees toward the grip; the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver in the bay underneath.

gallery.caption: From the rider's seat: the slim collar between the grip and the switch cube (grey: a stand-in; measure yours), the joystick under the thumb, the electronics bay underneath

The face, square-on from the grip side: the joystick in the middle, 2 buttons either side, each in its own cup with ridges between them (round inner buttons, pill-shaped outer ones); the only screw is a small one at its back end
Along the bar: the face is a cradle curved along your thumb's sweep, the joystick standing up in the middle
From above: 19 mm wide along the bar, in the gap between the grip and the switch cube
The bay under the bar, opened: the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver on edge side by side, its cap and gasket below
Taken apart: the cap, the cover, the keypad (also the seam's gasket), the switch board, the collar's two halves and the bay's cap

docs.label: README: what it does, how it's built, the wiring and the dash-bus messages

collar_top.name: Collar top
collar_top.what: The smooth body's upper half: the ring's top and the pod's lower part (tilted toward the grip) that holds the switch board, open at the low seam; the back screw's insert; the inside M2.5 joins it to the bottom half from the pod's floor
collar_top.material: ASA (PETG for a first try), 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

collar_bottom.name: Collar bottom (with the bay)
collar_bottom.what: The smooth body's lower half: the ring's bottom and the electronics bay (the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver on edge inside); 2 M2 inserts for its cap, the inside screw's M2.5 insert; the front screw comes up through it into the cover
collar_bottom.material: ASA / PETG, 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

pod_cover.name: Pod cover
pod_cover.what: The face and the pod's upper sides in one smooth part (no screws on the face): a thumb cradle curved along the thumb's sweep, a cup round each button and ridges between them. Held by an M2.5 from underneath at the front (into its insert) and a small countersunk M2.5 at its back end
pod_cover.material: ASA / PETG. Its flat underside down

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: A TPU liner inside the cover, in one piece: the sheet under the face (its hollow domes are the buttons (round inside, pills outside, their tops following the face's curve), it hugs the joystick cap's sleeve), a skirt that holds the switch board down, and a flange that is the seam's gasket
keypad.material: TPU 85A-95A. On its flange (open side down)

joy_cap.name: Joystick cap
joy_cap.what: A low 13 mm mushroom cap that pushes onto the 5-way switch's stem
joy_cap.material: ASA / PETG, or TPU for grip. Flat top down

bay_cap.name: Bay cap
bay_cap.what: A rounded dish that closes the bay from below (2 M2 x 6 countersunk); the dash's 4-core cable comes in through it

bay_gasket.name: Bay gasket
bay_gasket.what: Between the bay and its cap, squeezed 0.2 mm

remote_assembled.name: Assembled
remote_assembled.what: The collar on the bar, with stand-ins for the grip, the switch cube and the boards

params.name: buttons
params.label: Buttons
params.help: All in one row round the bar: the collar is too narrow for two rows.

params.name: gap_w
params.label: Gap between the grip and the switch cube
params.help: The collar is 1 mm narrower. Slide the switch cube inboard to make room.

params.name: pod_a
params.label: Where the controls face, round the bar
params.help: From straight forward: 90 = straight up, 125 = up and back toward your thumb. Up to 135 with 4 buttons.

params.name: pod_tilt
params.label: Controls tilted toward the grip
params.help: So your thumb reaches them straight from the grip.

params.name: nav_top
params.label: Joystick: the stem's top above its board
params.help: Too short and its cap can't grip it (the model says so).
